opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin requires owning role, which is Engineer; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level equals maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training (note says full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type). Contractor policy: read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Basic training => max read. Requested write is above max, so recommend read.
reason: Jennifer Miller (E017) requests write access to Source Code. The two notes conflict on employment type: the HR note says full-time, while the Security note says contractor (from the Security DB, which it states is authoritative for employment type) with basic security training. Under contractor policy, maximum access is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Since the requested write exceeds the contractor's maximum of read, I grant the maximum of read.
